title: neuron-lens catalog sample (Qwen3-8B, Gemma-4-12B)
attribution: neuron-lens catalog by @_a9lim and @treetowntree with Claude (Anthropic), 2026-10-31. Code: https://github.com/stdlogits/neuron-lens. Labels are model-written; confidences are theirs.
changes: Subset only: all head labels + legibility, and layer-8 neuron labels (highest writes_conf 300 per model) joined with their legibility row. Floats rounded to 3 dp. No text edited.

heads.fires: multilingual function-word and punctuation tokens in mixed-script text
heads.attends: previous-token-independent; diffuse, content keyed to Chinese/Persian/Romance function words
heads.writes: weak copy of diverse words; little clear promotion
heads.note: Layer 0, diffuse attention (sink 0.00, prev 0.04); OV copies broad multilingual tokens with score +0.99 but no dominant theme; low confidence.

heads.fires: tokens right after a word, mostly the current token in code and prose
heads.attends: the immediately previous token (prev-token head)
heads.writes: copies previous token's identity such as 'this', 'was', 'is', 'we'
heads.note: Previous-token score 0.82 dominates; OV copies function words and suppresses ellipsis/quote-newline tokens, a weak theme.

heads.fires: current token in self-repeating runs of punctuation and short words
heads.attends: itself, the current token (self-attention)
heads.writes: reinforces the current token; suppresses 'of', 'to' and quote-dash tokens
heads.note: Self-attention 0.64 and high self-seeking median z +3.19; attends to itself across copies of common tokens.

heads.fires: question marks, colons and full-width punctuation ending clauses
heads.attends: earlier punctuation tokens like '？', '。' and newline separators
heads.writes: copies sentence-level function words and suppresses adverbs
heads.note: Fires on Chinese question marks in driver contexts; OV copy score is high but the write is generic, so weak.

heads.fires: Arabic diacritics and rare-character tokens mid-text
heads.attends: previous token, typically a rare or diacritic character
heads.writes: suppresses punctuation and quote tokens such as ')' and ';'
heads.note: Drivers are diacritics and CJK garbage; OV suppresses code punctuation; the attention pattern is only moderately previous-token.

heads.fires: ampersand-entity and HTML-escape fragments like '&' and '&#'
heads.attends: earlier ampersand and entity-fragment tokens
heads.writes: copies ampersand and entity-starting tokens; suppresses punctuation
heads.note: Top copy list and drivers are '&' and '&#' entity fragments; self-seeking shows repeated words like 'at'.

heads.fires: word-internal fragments inside repeated multi-token words ('aest', 'het')
heads.attends: earlier fragments of the same split word
heads.writes: copies ellipsis and dot runs; suppresses capital-letter tokens
heads.note: Context examples show fragments of 'aesthetically' split across tokens; OV copies ellipses, a weak signal.

heads.fires: phrase-introducing words in prepositional context like 'at', 'and', 'like'
heads.attends: HTML entity fragments and earlier prepositions
heads.writes: copies adverbs and modifiers like 'just', 'very', 'like'
heads.note: Context shows 'at' before 'risk'; OV copies adverbs and suppresses prepositions, moderately consistent.

heads.fires: on 'should/shouldn/could/will' modal-like tokens and following words, e.g. 'shouldn't' context
heads.attends: modal verbs and negated modals (shouldn, couldn't) in prior text
heads.writes: copies modal/auxiliary-like tokens such as should, could, will, may
heads.note: Layer 0 OV copy score +1 with modal/ability words in copy list; contexts show shouldn't attended. Weak QK evidence beyond that.

heads.fires: on 'shouldn't/couldn't/can' negation-modal tokens, especially the 'n' stem before 't'
heads.attends: the token itself (self-attention) on modal and negated-modal words
heads.writes: copies modal and negated-modal tokens (shouldn, wouldn, couldn, could)
heads.note: Self-attention 0.68 with strong copy of shouldn/wouldn/could; drivers list many modals; contexts show shouldn't as query and key.

heads.fires: on sentence-ending punctuation and line breaks, e.g. '.', ':', newline tokens
heads.attends: previous token, typically punctuation or closing marks
heads.writes: weakly copies modal words 'would', 'might', 'could' and 'by'
heads.note: Low norm percentile and weak copy score; driver list is punctuation; contexts show adjective/noun descriptive phrases, unclear.

heads.fires: on modal and auxiliary tokens (could, can, will, gonna) and ellipsis/newline tokens
heads.attends: previous token and nearby modal or auxiliary words
heads.writes: copies modal verbs like could, can, will, would
heads.note: OV copy list dominated by modals; drivers mix newline/ellipsis tokens; moderate confidence.

heads.fires: on formal academic-essay connective and register words (Moreover, Indeed, Interestingly, Figure)
heads.attends: academic connectives and register words earlier in text
heads.writes: copies formal/academic words like important, interesting, Moreover, Figure, used
heads.note: QK favours essay-style connectives; OV copies formal adjectives and figure references; moderate evidence.

heads.fires: on tokens with mixed or unusual script, e.g. Cyrillic-lookalike letters and line breaks
heads.attends: unclear; attends to prior punctuation and function words
heads.writes: copies profanity-like and emphatic words (FUCK, shitty) weakly
heads.note: Weak evidence; OV copy list has profanity and dash-connectives, contexts show Cyrillic-lookalike letters.

heads.fires: on ellipsis and punctuation tokens such as '...', '…' and figure-reference tokens
heads.attends: unclear; ellipsis and bracket tokens earlier
heads.writes: copies ellipsis and formal-register words like significant, interesting, likely
heads.note: Copy list mixes ellipsis with academic adjectives; contexts show bracket tags; low confidence.

heads.fires: on code-comment and sentence-initial punctuation, e.g. quote and closing-paren tokens
heads.attends: itself, the current token, on punctuation and code-start tokens
heads.writes: copies punctuation and quote-like tokens (’, ‘, —, ”)
heads.note: Self-attention 0.64 and self-seeking high on code/comment starts; OV copies typographic quotes and dashes.

heads.fires: Mid-word subword fragments and colloquial/informal word pieces
heads.attends: Previous token, mostly; weak content match
heads.writes: Weak copy of attended token, mainly common English function words and mid-word pieces
heads.note: Previous-token pattern (0.23) with flat OV copy score; contexts show ⟦qu⟧ after collo⟪⟫ but evidence is thin at layer 0.

heads.fires: Tokens right after line-start 'Answer' or 'As'/'Similar' openers in text
heads.attends: Previous token, with weak match to 'Answer' and sentence-opening words
heads.writes: Weak copy of previous-token word forms, mostly English words
heads.note: Previous-token pattern; contexts show ⟪Answer⟫ and ⟪ As⟫ attended, but copy score is near-neutral and the head is unclear.

heads.fires: Garbled or byte-fragment tokens and sentence-opening words like 'As', 'Answer'
heads.attends: Itself, the current token (self-attention)
heads.writes: Copies the current token, mostly function words and odd fragments
heads.note: Self-attention 0.55 and high self-seeking median z; OV copy score +1.00 but read is unclear beyond the self-attend pattern.

heads.fires: Sentence-opening words 'As', 'Even', 'Only', 'Such' before a continuation
heads.attends: Previous token, the word just before
heads.writes: Copies previous-token words like 'even', 'only', 'due' forward
heads.note: Previous-token pattern 0.21; contexts show ⟪As⟫⟦soon⟧ but drivers are varied; low confidence.

heads.fires: 'There' and 'However' sentence openers, and indent-whitespace runs
heads.attends: Previous token, typically a sentence-opening word like 'There' or 'However'
heads.writes: Suppresses repeated single-letter and symbol tokens; weak copy of 'there'
heads.note: Previous-token 0.29; contexts show ⟪There⟫ and ⟪However⟫ as attended; OV suppresses single letters and punctuation.

heads.fires: Indentation whitespace runs and 'However'/'Nevertheless' openers
heads.attends: Itself and whitespace or indentation tokens
heads.writes: Suppresses single-letter tokens and common words like 'and' and 'that'
heads.note: Self-attention 0.36; drivers are whitespace runs; OV suppresses single-letter and function-word tokens.

heads.fires: Digit and capital-letter tokens inside hex IDs and list markers
heads.attends: Itself, the current token; capitalised or digit tokens
heads.writes: Copies pronouns and digit or letter tokens such as 'you', 'they', '7'
heads.note: Self-attention 0.77 and self-seeking median z +3.21; OV copies pronouns and tokens like 'there', 'they', 'you'.

heads.fires: 'There' and 'much' contexts, and digit tokens, after a sentence opener
heads.attends: Previous token, with a weak match to 'There' openers
heads.writes: Suppresses digit tokens; copies first-person pronouns like 'we' and 'I'
heads.note: Previous-token 0.22; OV suppresses digits and punctuation, copies pronoun forms; contexts show ⟪There⟫ attended.

heads.fires: question-opening words (What, If, How, Let) and early-text tokens in prose
heads.attends: previous token and nearby punctuation or question-opener words
heads.writes: copies its attended token mildly; little clear promotion
heads.note: Layer-0 head with previous-token weight 0.25 and QK favouring What/If/How; OV copy score near +1 but weak read; low confidence overall.

heads.fires: tokens inside lists of named entities and sexual or political proper nouns (Mayweather, Pornhub)
heads.attends: sentence-ending punctuation and line breaks in the following text
heads.writes: promotes common function words (the, and, in) after copying them
heads.note: OV·R copies function words and self-seeks on 'With'; drivers are named entities; QK favours sentence punctuation; weak evidence.

heads.fires: repeated quote-openers and question words (What, When, For) and indentation runs
heads.attends: itself, the same token, mostly in code indent or quote-opener runs
heads.writes: copies the current token, reinforcing quote and question openers
heads.note: Self-attention 0.62 and self-seeking median z +3.47 mark a duplicate-token head; OV copies openers like What/When.

heads.fires: technical and academic topic nouns (data, research, students, Jesus, programming)
heads.attends: code-header and scripture-style tokens such as import, #include, Title
heads.writes: promotes topic nouns like student, physicist, computational, Jesus
heads.note: OV·R copies domain nouns and QK favours code and document headers; moderate evidence, mid-layer reads unreliable.

heads.fires: negative contractions (weren, aren, didn, couldn) and long whitespace runs
heads.attends: itself, repeated first names and the same token
heads.writes: copies the current token, e.g. contractions and names
heads.note: Self-seeking median z +5.68 at 97th percentile: strong duplicate-token head on names and whitespace; OV copies its own token.

heads.fires: whitespace runs and contraction or verb-form tokens after them
heads.attends: repeated first names and the same token
heads.writes: copies the current token, mostly names and whitespace
heads.note: Self-seeking median z +4.30 on male names and whitespace; duplicate-token profile; OV copy score near +1.

heads.fires: copula and auxiliary verbs (were, was, are, is) after subjects
heads.attends: the previous token, often a copula or auxiliary
heads.writes: promotes copulas and auxiliaries were, was, are
heads.note: Copies were/was/are/is in OV·S and copula drivers; previous-token weight 0.19 supports a local read.

heads.fires: word-level prose tokens after the first clause (distinguish, hesitate, chips)
heads.attends: previous token and sentence-starting words
heads.writes: promotes generic function words and punctuation
heads.note: Mostly weak: copy score near +1 with diffuse OV reads; drivers look unrelated; low confidence.

heads.fires: Tokens right before a line break or paragraph break, and sentence-final punctuation before ⏎⏎
heads.attends: Previous token, mostly closing punctuation or '.⏎⏎'-style boundaries
heads.writes: Weak: boosts function words like can/could/we/what after breaks
heads.note: Previous-token attention (0.12) with a copy-leaning OV footprint on ordinary words; QK favours ')./.⏎⏎' boundary tokens; drivers are Chinese demonstrative/quantity phrases. Low confidence.

heads.fires: Words that start a new clause or question, e.g. 'how', 'when', 'and', after 'and'/'how' contexts
heads.attends: The previous token, typically a conjunction or wh-word like 'and how'
heads.writes: Mild push toward clause-linking words (and, but, when, because)
heads.note: Contexts show '⟪how⟫⟦it⟧' pattern on previous token; OV copies 'and/but/when'; footprint is modest and QK is unclear.

heads.fires: Sentence-initial subject or adverb tokens ('it', 'there', 'Due', 'Also') before an infinitive or predicate
heads.attends: The previous token, often a subject pronoun like 'it' or a sentence opener
heads.writes: Promotes auxiliaries and copulas (was, were, could, has, is)
heads.note: Context '⟪it⟫'s important⟦to⟧' and copy list of 'there, it, was, could' point to subject-to-predicate prediction; previous-token attention 0.18.

heads.fires: Chinese province and city names, and European-language tokens mid-phrase
heads.attends: The previous token, often a place-name or import-statement fragment
heads.writes: Weak: promotes Romance/Germanic function words (je, é, ou, este)
heads.note: Drivers are Chinese place names; copy list is mostly non-English function words; low-norm, weak evidence.

heads.fires: Tokens inside code or math expressions, e.g. brackets, subscripts, identifiers mid-token
heads.attends: The immediately previous token (previous-token score 0.74)
heads.writes: Promotes math/code closers and subscripts (_{, frac, ), }, ))
heads.note: Strong previous-token attention; OV copies LaTeX and bracket closers such as '_{', 'frac', ')'; output is large at most positions.

heads.fires: Determiners and quantifiers before a noun ('the', 'another', 'a', 'a 个')
heads.attends: The previous token, often a noun phrase head or a classifier
heads.writes: Promotes 'the' and determiners such as 'the', 'in', 'their'
heads.note: Copy list led by 'the×10', 'in', 'its', 'their'; drivers include 'another' and Chinese 个 classifier contexts.

heads.fires: Plural determiners and pronouns like 'those', 'they', 'are' before a participle
heads.attends: The previous token, typically 'those' or a subject noun
heads.writes: Promotes copulas and plural pronouns (are, have, were, they, those)
heads.note: Contexts center on '⟪those⟫⟦affected⟧'; copy list is verbs of be/have plus pronouns; drivers are adverbs before verbs.

heads.fires: Closing brackets and parentheses inside code, e.g. ')', ']', '})' in nested expressions
heads.attends: The previous token, often a bracket or a name before a closer
heads.writes: Promotes closing brackets and punctuation like ')', '}', '))'
heads.note: Copy list is dominated by ')', '}', ')))', and fractional/LaTeX tokens; a low-norm head with bracket-focused QK.

heads.fires: Mid-sentence and after punctuation tokens in prose; weak, diffuse firing
heads.attends: Previous token, mostly after punctuation or newline-heavy text
heads.writes: Weak output; copies closing-bracket/code-ish tokens and suppresses words like children, likely
heads.note: Low prev-token and sink scores; OV copy score near zero; contexts show no clear pattern. Layer 1 reads are weak.

heads.fires: Chinese noun and phrase tokens in running text, e.g. 春运, 火锅, 别墅
heads.attends: Previous token and content words before a colon or key label, e.g. 'Author:' or 'Filename'
heads.writes: Copies content tokens like children, folks, students, money, teacher; suppresses newline and quote tokens
heads.note: OV·S and OV·R both copy (+0.98, +0.57); QK favours newline-ending tokens; drivers are Chinese nouns and English topic nouns.

heads.fires: Opening-quote and code-comment tokens like triple quotes and newlines
heads.attends: Triple-quote and newline tokens (""" and ''' delimiters) in code and docstrings
heads.writes: Copies discourse adverbs like additionally, therefore, significant; suppresses single capital letters
heads.note: OV·S copy score +0.86 with adverb list; QK strongly on docstring delimiters; self-seeking low.

heads.fires: Programming identifiers and class names like TypeError, AuthService, QLineEdit, and math topic words
heads.attends: Code and math topic keywords such as Lemma, Mathematics, def, Implement, and code delimiters
heads.writes: Copies math and symbol tokens like $, Number, teams, economic; suppresses single capital letters
heads.note: Drivers are code class names; QK top keys are math and programming headers; OV copy score +0.91.

heads.fires: Word-internal fragments in subword-split text, e.g. mid-word pieces
heads.attends: Current token itself and previous token; word-fragment pieces
heads.writes: Copies word-fragment subword pieces like urg, erg, ent, ist, ord
heads.note: Self-attention 0.18 and OV copy score +0.99 on fragments; output promotes subword continuations.

heads.fires: Chinese characters in the middle of multi-character words, and split-character names
heads.attends: Previous token, often a Chinese character or word-internal fragment
heads.writes: Copies word-piece fragments and Chinese characters; suppresses function words like is, in, for
heads.note: Context examples are Chinese word splits; OV copy +0.94 with suppression of common English function words.

heads.fires: The 'only' in 'Not only ... but also' constructions and similar correlative pairs
heads.attends: The 'Not' and 'only' tokens earlier in correlative 'not only ... but' sentences
heads.writes: Suppresses quote-ending and ellipsis tokens; weakly copies 'and', 'the', 'of'
heads.note: Context cards show 'Not only' pairs as keys; OV copy score negative (-0.69), so it suppresses what it reads.

heads.fires: Chinese verb-complement and directional tokens such as 出, 过, 起, 下 after verbs
heads.attends: Previous token, a Chinese verb or character in a compound
heads.writes: Copies Chinese word-fragment characters and some Latin subword pieces; suppresses 'and', 'the'
heads.note: Drivers are Chinese verb-complement characters; OV copy +0.97 with suppression of English function words.

heads.fires: Verb or auxiliary right after a relative/subject pronoun (that, they, which)
heads.attends: Relative or subject pronouns like 'that', 'they', 'which' before a verb
heads.writes: Pushes pronouns and determiners (they, it, that, which, you) forward
heads.note: Contexts show query verbs ('be', 'need') attending to the preceding 'that'/'they'. OV·S copies pronouns; OV·R suppresses adverbs and brackets. Weak at layer 1.

heads.fires: Tokens following a wh-question word in a question clause
heads.attends: Wh-words such as 'what', 'how', 'why' earlier in the clause
heads.writes: Weak push toward wh-words and 'is/the' in question continuations
heads.note: Contexts show 'and what' attended from 'is'/'these'. OV·S copies question words like 'What', 'How', 'Why', but the evidence is thin.

heads.fires: Second occurrence of a repeated named entity or multi-token term
heads.attends: Earlier mention of the same entity or term (Qaeda, Ebola, GDPR)
heads.writes: Copies discourse connectives (however, so, because, therefore)
heads.note: Self-seeking median z +1.53 and duplicate score 0.11. Contexts show repeated names. OV·S copies connectives; OV·R suppresses 'the', 'you', 'and'.

heads.fires: Repeated character or token inside a reduplicated CJK or word sequence
heads.attends: Earlier identical token in the same local span (duplicate-token copy)
heads.writes: Pushes math and code symbols ($, \(, {, =) and suppresses 'the' and commas
heads.note: Strongest self-seeking (median z +4.84, duplicate 0.19). Contexts show a repeated CJK character attended to the earlier copy. Output is unclear.

heads.fires: Token after a repeated line-start symbol in code, or 的 in Chinese phrases
heads.attends: Earlier identical symbol at line start such as '@@' or '#'
heads.writes: Copies code operators and keywords (=>, (b, select, +=)
heads.note: Contexts mix '@@' code lines and '的' phrases. OV·S copies code tokens; the head is self-seeking on newline-run punctuation. Weak evidence.

heads.fires: Chinese adverbs and discourse words (這樣, 當然, 同時) and comment-start tokens
heads.attends: Sentence-initial discourse connectives and '#' comment markers
heads.writes: Copies sentence-initial connectives (Thus, Therefore, However, But, Yet)
heads.note: OV·S copies discourse openers like Thus, Therefore, But; OV·R suppresses ellipsis and quote tokens. Contexts show '#' comments attended.

heads.fires: Japanese and Chinese content tokens, and text just after a newline run
heads.attends:
Newline-run and closing-punctuation tokens such as ')

' and '.

'
heads.writes: Promotes newline-run and paragraph-break tokens (⏎⏎) after punctuation
heads.note: OV·R copies '⏎⏎' and closing quote/paren runs; QK favours '.⏎⏎' keys. Contexts are scattered, so firing is low-confidence.

heads.fires: Punctuation and line-end boundaries in code or quoted prose
heads.attends: Statement-end tokens like ');' or adverbs 'really', 'just', 'rather'
heads.writes: Copies adverbs and commas (more, really, just, like); suppresses newline runs
heads.note: OV·R copies 'more', 'really', 'just' and ',...' while suppressing '⏎⏎⏎'. Contexts show code '#' comment lines, but the pattern is weak.

heads.fires: Closing brackets and quotes in runs of code or prose, e.g. ')))' and '"))'
heads.attends: Tokens after line breaks in code or prose, mainly ')' and '.' before double newlines
heads.writes: Promotes closing-bracket and quote tokens like ')', '}', '])'
heads.note: OV·S copies closers strongly; drivers are opening/closing bracket runs; attention pattern is diffuse, weak evidence.

heads.fires: Closing brackets and quotes inside code calls, e.g. '))' and '])' in os.path chains
heads.attends: Nearby code tokens inside nested call expressions, such as 'os', '(' and 'path'
heads.writes: Promotes closing brackets and quote tokens such as ')', '}', ']'
heads.note: OV·S copies closing punctuation; drivers and contexts are nested-parenthesis code; attention weakly on code openers.

heads.fires: Tokens right before a list or conjunction, e.g. 'or', 'and', ':', '—' in mixed prose
heads.attends: Connector tokens 'example', 'such as', 'or' and 'the' right before a repeated phrase
heads.writes: Weakly promotes closing parentheses and sentence-final tokens
heads.note: Mixed signals; OV·S copies common words and closers; contexts show 'For example, instead of' connectors; low confidence.

heads.fires: Closing brackets and newline runs after code or prose, e.g. ')⏎⏎' and '⏎⏎'
heads.attends: Previous closing or sentence tokens in code and prose
heads.writes: Weakly promotes closing brackets and modal words like 'will', 'may'
heads.note: Output copy list is closers; suppresses 'math'-like tokens; weak evidence overall.

heads.fires: Mid-name tokens in Chinese and English proper names, e.g. surname or name fragments
heads.attends: Earlier token of the same multi-token name or entity, e.g. '金山', '奥巴'
heads.writes: Promotes repeats of earlier name fragments by copying the attended name token
heads.note: Strong duplicate-token pattern (0.95) with contexts showing repeated entity names; copy score is low, so writes is weak.

heads.fires: Chinese or unusual single-character tokens inside names and transliterations
heads.attends: Previous-token or nearby characters in transliterated names, e.g. '洛', '尼斯'
heads.writes: Suppresses hedge adverbs such as 'now', 'perhaps', 'further', 'often'
heads.note: OV·R suppresses adverbs and hedges; the contexts are noisy transliterations; unclear.

heads.fires: Capitalised name starts and rare word-initial fragments, e.g. 'Opr', 'Obl', 'Hatch'
heads.attends: Previous token in names, e.g. '奥' before '巴' in Chinese transliterations
heads.writes: Promotes capital-letter name fragments and uppercase tokens like 'TC', 'TT', 'TN'
heads.note: OV·R copies capitalised fragments strongly; contexts are name transliterations; moderate-low confidence.

heads.fires: Tokens ending a statement before a closing paren or semicolon in code, e.g. ';' and '();'
heads.attends: Earlier duplicate of the current token, especially repeated name fragments and identifiers
heads.writes: Suppresses sentence-final and connective words like 'in', 'and', 'the', 'of'
heads.note: Duplicate-token attention (0.96); OV·R suppresses connectives and copies modal and hedge words; weak evidence on writes.

heads.fires: closing brackets and quotes in code and prose, e.g. ']{', ')\n\n', '}"'
heads.attends: opening brackets and parentheses; self-seeking on '{' and '(' tokens
heads.writes: weak copy of bracket/quote-like tokens; suppresses plain words
heads.note: Mean QK favours closers like ')))' and self-seeking on '{', '('; OV·S copy score is mild and the layer reads are weak at this depth.

heads.fires: tokens before runs of closing brackets or nationality/country names in lists
heads.attends: runs of closing parens '))' and '));' in code
heads.writes: weak; suppresses quote-plus-newline endings
heads.note: QK favours '))' closers and self-seeks on them; driver list is mixed (country names, '("/"'), so confidence is low.

heads.fires: HTML tag starts like '<script', '<form', '<div' in markup
heads.attends: closing brackets and '}]' runs; self-seeks on '{' and '}' tokens
heads.writes: copies bracket and tag-opening tokens such as '</', '{', '['
heads.note: Drivers are clearly HTML '<' tags; the attended key side is bracket-heavy closers and openers, with self-seeking on braces.

heads.fires: content words after 'the' or 'to' in academic prose (purpose, people, sensitive)
heads.attends: Chinese news and topic phrases, weakly; closers in code
heads.writes: weak copy of mixed foreign-language function words
heads.note: Driver list is mostly Chinese content words with no crisp theme; the OV copy list is diffuse.

heads.fires: word after 'a bit' or 'similar' in comparison phrases ('like', 'to')
heads.attends: the word 'like' or 'to' in comparison constructions; opening quote-parens
heads.writes: copies sentence-final quote and newline tokens; suppresses opening parens
heads.note: Context examples show 'a bit like' and 'similar to' comparisons; OV copy list is end-of-quote tokens.

heads.fires: tokens inside repeated quoted or code passages; first-word adjectives after 'more'
heads.attends: earlier copy of the current token (duplicate-token head)
heads.writes: copies adjectives and comparison words like 'more', 'critical', 'should'
heads.note: Duplicate score 0.71 and self-seeking z +4.6 mark a duplicate-token head; output theme is weakly adjectival.

heads.fires: word after a question word ('How', 'What', 'Who') in a question
heads.attends: the subject pronoun or 'you' after a question word; previous token
heads.writes: copies modal and function words like 'should', 'must', 'more'
heads.note: Contexts show question-start tokens with the next subject word attended; previous-token score 0.09 is the highest of the pattern measures.

heads.fires: sentence-initial discourse words ('Moreover', 'What', 'Then', 'Additionally') and Chinese quantifier phrases
heads.attends: the previous token; closing-paren and ')' runs in code
heads.writes: copies transitional adverbs and connectives such as 'Moreover', 'Furthermore', 'Additionally'
heads.note: OV copy list is dominated by discourse connectives like Moreover, Furthermore, Therefore; contexts are mixed, so confidence is moderate.

heads.fires: Mid-sentence content tokens inside clauses; weak, diffuse firing across text
heads.attends: Tokens right after a repeated opening such as 'Christ', 'Copyright', 'Torah'
heads.writes: Suppresses British spellings and formal/hedging adverbs like 'enthusiasm', 'thereby'
heads.note: OV·S copying score is negative and suppression list is mixed; contexts are heterogeneous, so low confidence throughout.

heads.fires: Transition and connective adverbs starting clauses: 'therefore', 'Furthermore', 'Moreover', 'Consequently'
heads.attends: Dotted ellipsis and punctuation runs ('.....', '────', '→') in later positions
heads.writes: Promotes formal connectives ('therefore', 'Furthermore', 'indeed') and suppresses digits and 'and'
heads.note: OV·S copying score is high (97th pct) and the copy list is dominated by connective adverbs; attention targets are weak.

heads.fires: Proper nouns naming places, nationalities or cultures (e.g. 中国, 京都, Estonian)
heads.attends: Suffixes and inflections after a stem, e.g. 'ian', 'et', 'isi' in multilingual text
heads.writes: Weak; slightly promotes common function words and suppresses hedging connectives
heads.note: Driver tokens are place and national names; output read is near zero, so the write is unclear.

heads.fires: Adverbs and modifiers after a clause ('anyways', 'subsequently', 'drastically', 'almost')
heads.attends: Closing punctuation and quote-newline tokens before a new line
heads.writes: Mildly promotes adverbs and hedges; suppresses digits and code punctuation
heads.note: Copy list leans toward adverbs and suppression toward digits and code symbols; attention targets are weak.

heads.fires: Nouns in lists of roles or topics ('writers', 'Actors', 'presenter', 'Reporter')
heads.attends: Plural role nouns and list-item words that repeat earlier in a biography or listing
heads.writes: Promotes plural role and profession nouns; suppresses punctuation and 'the'
heads.note: Key-side driver tokens are role nouns; output copy list is mixed and attention is diffuse.

heads.fires: Code identifiers and API names (QWidget, urlpatterns, BeautifulSoup, Vocabulary)
heads.attends: Earlier identical or near-identical word (duplicate-token look-back, e.g. 'paper' in 'Paperback')
heads.writes: Promotes content nouns and topic words such as 'health', 'community', 'legal'; weak
heads.note: Duplicate score is highest of the group (0.10) and self-seeking z is high; write is modest.

heads.fires: Code and indentation tokens in programming contexts (argsort, ElementsByTagName)
heads.attends: Earlier code identifiers and keywords within the same snippet
heads.writes: Promotes paragraph-break and ellipsis tokens ('...⏎⏎', '⏎⏎⏎')
heads.note: OV·R copying is strongest for multi-newline and ellipsis tokens; attention targets are code keywords.

heads.fires: Tokens in chemistry, graphics and tech-product names (QWidget, Photoshop, piano)
heads.attends: Period or question mark closing a title-like heading (e.g. 'Ever After is So Once Upon a Time.')
heads.writes: Suppresses clause punctuation and 'the'; weak positive for quote marks
heads.note: Self-seeking is strongly negative, so it avoids repeating tokens; contexts are scattered and output read is weak.

heads.fires: Closing brackets and quotes before newlines in code; also stray quote/dash tokens
heads.attends:
Closing code delimiters like ))
 and ]
; self-matching punctuation runs
heads.writes: Mildly copies attended token; weak, unclear output direction
heads.note:
Self-seeking and QK lists favour )

-style closers; OV copy score is modest (+0.79 OV·S, +0.17 OV·R). Weak evidence overall.

heads.fires: Sentence-level discourse connectives and adverbs (therefore, moreover, thus) and code closers
heads.attends: Closing code brackets and block ends like }, and }); before newlines
heads.writes: Weakly copies connective/transition words; unclear
heads.note: QK·S favours adverbs like Interestingly, Moreover; key side favours }); closers. Output norm is low; read is weak.

heads.fires: Tokens inside URLs, bug-tracker paths and code identifiers mid-sentence
heads.attends: Closing parentheses and ]\n\n-style code endings
heads.writes: Suppresses dashes, em-dashes and common function words when read
heads.note: OV copy score negative (-0.29 OV·S, -0.31 OV·R); suppresses —that/—or-type tokens. Contexts show URL/path tokens.

heads.fires: Ellipses and em-dashes joining clauses (…, —that, —who)
heads.attends: Previous token, with a bias toward closing brackets and code closers
heads.writes: Copies ellipsis and em-dash tokens forward; suppresses plain clause connectives
heads.note: OV·R copies …, ’s, —that strongly; suppresses this, these, when, so. Drivers include rare punctuation tokens.

heads.fires: Timestamp colons and times in logs; also Chinese phrase-initial tokens
heads.attends: Digits and colons in timestamps; code closers like ');
heads.writes: Copies assorted word-initial tokens; suppresses closing code brackets
heads.note: Context examples are timestamp colons (09⟪:⟫07). Suppresses ')\n and '))\n tokens; copy score +0.94 OV·S.

heads.fires: Chinese content nouns and topic words (sports, technology, adult-topic nouns)
heads.attends: Timestamp digits and the second occurrence of a repeated token (duplicate)
heads.writes: Copies topical nouns (sports, technology, military, health) forward
heads.note: OV·R copies topic nouns like football, cancer, military, network; duplicate-attention 0.19 is notable. Context evidence mixed.

heads.fires: Prepositional phrases starting with 在 (在上海, 在家, 在网上) and French se-verbs
heads.attends: Previous token and the closing ');\n tokens of code
heads.writes: Copies function words like be, are, were, after; mild suppression of programme/licence
heads.note: Drivers are 在+place phrases; OV·S copies auxiliaries (be, were, have). Contexts show French and Indonesian morphology.

heads.fires: Subword fragments inside multi-token words (Indonesian pem-, meng-, code identifiers)
heads.attends: Partial word prefixes and code closers like "]);\n
heads.writes: Copies subword fragments and technical word-pieces forward
heads.note: Contexts are word-continuation pieces (pem⟫aka⟫ian, peng⟫guna); OV·S copies many word-piece and sub-token items.

heads.fires: Mid-sentence adverb/verb positions after 'largely'/'been' and in repeated-punctuation tails; weak, diffuse
heads.attends: Previous token, mainly punctuation or closing-bracket tokens before newlines
heads.writes: Weak copy of mixed punctuation and word-end tokens; no clear promotion
heads.note: Previous-token weight 0.23 but OV copy score only +0.69 with no coherent token theme; weak early-layer head.

heads.fires: Tokens right before a preposition or infinitive like 为/提供 in Chinese and 'might/have' in English
heads.attends: Previous token; Chinese function-word and modal contexts
heads.writes: Promotes modal and auxiliary English words (might, have, has, should) and some Chinese verbs
heads.note: OV·S copy list has modals and auxiliaries (might, has, should) with mid-layer copy score; contexts show 为/提供 patterns.

heads.fires: Comma and list-punctuation tokens in code (',message', ',number') and 'both' contexts
heads.attends: Previous token, often a comma or closing bracket before a newline in code
heads.writes: Copies comma and bracket-closing tokens and suppresses articles like 'the'
heads.note: Drivers are predominantly commas in code; suppression list is articles (the, an, A), a consistent theme in OV·S.

heads.fires: Code-ish slash and ampersand tokens in URLs, and 'one of the' phrasing
heads.attends: Previous token and code/URL punctuation
heads.writes: Unclear; weakly copies '-the' and suppresses punctuation
heads.note: Drivers mix URL slashes, Chinese nouns and 'one of' contexts with no single theme.

heads.fires: Chinese noun and topic tokens in news-style text, and identifier suffixes like '_s' or '_pub'
heads.attends: Earlier copies of the current token (duplicate-token attention)
heads.writes: Suppresses repeated punctuation and quote tokens; no clear promotion
heads.note: Duplicate score 0.79 and self-seeking median z +4.37 mark a duplicate-token head; OV copy score strongly negative.

heads.fires: Mid-sentence content words in English and Chinese prose, and 'ridiculous' style adjectives
heads.attends: Attention-sink position 0; otherwise diffuse
heads.writes: Ellipsis tokens copied forward ('...' and '...⏎'); suppresses function words
heads.note: Copy-most list dominated by ellipsis variants; suppress list is function words like that, to, the.

heads.fires: Chinese and English nouns in headline-style and topic-title contexts
heads.attends: Start-of-text sink and '#' or '?' heading markers before newlines
heads.writes: Copies closing parentheses and quotes; suppresses newline runs
heads.note: Output norm very low; copy list is closing brackets and quotes, suppress list is blank-line runs.

heads.fires: Subword continuation pieces inside split words, e.g. '斯' or 'ner' in names and places
heads.attends: Earlier tokens that began the same word, the token after an earlier copy (induction)
heads.writes: Promotes word-ending suffix pieces (ing, es, ed, ers, ity, ness)
heads.note: Induction score 0.86 and OV·R copy list of suffixes (ing, ed, ness, ity) are strong, consistent evidence.

heads.fires: Inside code, on getter-style identifiers like getX, getValue, getElement
heads.attends: Earlier identifiers and code tokens like getX, glColor, showDialog in code
heads.writes: Closing brackets and parens like ')' ']' '}' in code context

heads.fires: Sentence-initial quoted or adjective-like words after newlines and openers
heads.attends: Newline runs and closing punctuation, sink-like context
heads.writes: Copies closing parens and brackets; weak generic copying

heads.fires: Closing parens and brackets ending code or quoted phrases
heads.attends: Previous token, mostly closing parentheses in code
heads.writes: Copies closing parens and brackets like ')' and '))'

heads.fires: Words following a function word or auxiliary, mid-sentence adverbs and verbs
heads.attends: Previous token, strongly (0.45)
heads.writes: Copies closing parens and brackets; previous-token signal

heads.fires: Mid-sentence function words and verbs after contractions and quoted fragments
heads.attends: Sink position and content words in prose
heads.writes: Weak copying of quotes and punctuation; unclear

heads.fires: Repeated identifier tokens within code imports and names
heads.attends: Earlier copy of the same token (duplicate-token attention)
heads.writes: Weak copying of the attended token; little promotion

heads.fires: Repeated name or word tokens on a second mention
heads.attends: Earlier occurrence of the same token, duplicate-token attention
heads.writes: Suppresses the repeated token; copy-suppression of repeats

heads.fires: Repeated name or word tokens on a second mention
heads.attends: Earlier occurrence of the same token, duplicate-token attention
heads.writes: Suppresses the repeated token; copy-suppression of repeats

heads.fires: Mid-word or mid-phrase fragments inside multilingual text, e.g. Chinese or Latin-script pieces
heads.attends: Rare multilingual subword pieces and code-like tokens, not a fixed earlier copy
heads.writes: Promotes formal connective and adverb words (however, therefore, indeed, certainly)
heads.note: OV·S copy list is dominated by formal adverbs and connectives (Furthermore, however, therefore); drivers are scattered foreign fragments, so fires is weak.

heads.fires: Chinese characters and rare subword pieces mid-word, e.g. 東, 園, ascii fragments
heads.attends: Code closers and punctuation runs like ')); and '"' in code
heads.writes: Suppresses common words and spelling variants when they recur (copy suppression)
heads.note: OV·R and OV·S are negative (suppresses most); attention to code closers is clear from the key drivers.

heads.fires: Positions right after a question-mark-and-newline break or a sentence-ending period
heads.attends: The '?' and newline markers that close a question in FAQ-style text
heads.writes: Pushes down common function and emotive words; little clear promotion
heads.note: Context examples all show attention to a '?⏎⏎' boundary; OV reads are weakly suppressive, so writes is a guess.

heads.fires: Proper nouns and named entities, e.g. politicians, companies, celebrities
heads.attends: Named-entity tokens and programming API names like QWidget, JSONObject
heads.writes: Promotes nouns from sports, religion and politics such as Bible, Jesus, NFL
heads.note: Drivers are almost all named entities; OV·R copy list is a theme of sports, church and politics nouns.

heads.fires: Words beginning a noun phrase, such as after 'the' or a proper-name fragment
heads.attends: Itself or an earlier identical token: strong duplicate-token attention
heads.writes: Copies repeated tokens in duplicated names and words, weakly
heads.note: Duplicate attention is 0.87 and self-seeking z is high; output effect is small (copy score near zero).

heads.fires: Punctuation and closers ending a line, e.g. ')' and '.' before blank lines
heads.attends: Earlier identical closing tokens of code and list items
heads.writes: Suppresses quote and em-dash tokens such as ”, —he, ...
heads.note: OV·R suppresses quote and dash tokens; attention pattern is sink-heavy and weak, so labels are low confidence.

heads.fires: Numbered list items and digits in enumerated lists
heads.attends: Earlier identical digits or list-closing tokens, e.g. ')' in code
heads.writes: Suppresses ellipses and quote marks at line ends
heads.note: Context examples show digit tokens in numbered lists; duplicate attention 0.58 supports attending to earlier copies.

heads.fires: Tokens inside a repeated phrase or name that has appeared earlier
heads.attends: Earlier identical tokens (duplicate), often a name or code closer
heads.writes: Weak output; mildly promotes wordy nouns and affixes like -ness, -ity
heads.note: Duplicate attention 0.87 is strong; output promotion is weak and mixed.

heads.fires: code identifiers and closing bracket/quote runs; Chinese and Western tokens with no clear theme
heads.attends: closing punctuation runs like newlines after brackets, and earlier name-like tokens
heads.writes: weak; mixed copy of code suffixes and punctuation, suppresses function words
heads.note: Output norm moderate; OV·S copy score mildly positive, OV·R weak; QK favours closing-bracket-newline keys. Layer 3 is low-confidence.

heads.fires: quoted-speech closers and code bracket runs, with mixed tokens
heads.attends: closing quote and paragraph-break tokens (”⏎⏎, )⏎⏎)
heads.writes: suppresses closing brackets and quote tokens (anti-copy of punctuation)
heads.note: OV·R copy score negative with quote-closer tokens copied and dashes suppressed; QK favours paragraph-end punctuation. Weak band.

heads.fires: verbs and auxiliaries after subjects, and Chinese adverb-of-frequency phrases
heads.attends: previous content words and pronouns like we, you, was
heads.writes: promotes auxiliaries and pronouns (was, were, our, you) when copying
heads.note: OV·S and OV·R copy score positive, copying was/were/are and you/we; high firing fraction; layer-3 read.

heads.fires: repeated phrase second occurrences, especially the word after a repeated verb or name
heads.attends: earlier duplicate of the current token (duplicate-token head)
heads.writes: copies earlier duplicate tokens and interjections like ellipses and ⏎⏎
heads.note: Duplicate attention 0.25 is the highest signal; self-seeking median z high; write reads are weak.

heads.fires: tokens in pornographic or spam-keyword lists and Chinese medical product terms
heads.attends: encyclopedia-style header words and preceding titles
heads.writes: copies ellipses, em-dashes and newline runs
heads.note: Output norm high but firing sparse; OV reads weakly copy punctuation; source contexts are heterogeneous.

heads.fires: numerals and proper names in lists (countries, nationalities, digits)
heads.attends: list-entry tokens like digits and nationality adjectives
heads.writes: suppresses function words and punctuation like ellipses
heads.note: Drivers include digits and ethnic/national adjectives; OV reads weak; QK self-seeking modest.

heads.fires: tokens following a Chinese or English discourse connective, and technology brand names
heads.attends: previous discourse markers and conjunctions
heads.writes: copies conjunctions and adverbs like and, that, just, also
heads.note: OV·S copy score high; OV·R copies connectives and conversational words; layer-3 band.

heads.fires: city, country and surname names at the start of a proper noun phrase
heads.attends: previous capitalized name tokens (place names, sports teams)
heads.writes: suppresses dashes and whitespace-run tokens
heads.note: Drivers are place and team names; OV·R strongly negative, suppressing dashes; weak evidence.

heads.fires: Mid-word or code-fragment tokens inside quoted strings and brackets, before closing punctuation
heads.attends: Previous tokens; weak, diffuse; code closers and punctuation favoured as keys
heads.writes: Boosts code-closing punctuation and syntax tokens like ';', ')', '}'
heads.note: Copies code punctuation via OV·S (copy score +0.47); attention is diffuse with no strong previous-token or induction pattern; drivers are weak and mixed.

heads.fires: Function-word tokens like 'for', 'at', 'with', 'by', 'have' in running English
heads.attends: The previous token, mostly; closing brackets and quotes as keys
heads.writes: Copies prepositions and auxiliaries like 'for', 'with', 'by', 'have', 'take'
heads.note: OV·S copies 'for', 'at', 'with', 'by' strongly (score +0.86); previous-token attention 0.12; QK drivers are noisy, so the attends label is weaker.

heads.fires: Scattered tokens in mixed-language text; no clear theme
heads.attends: Its own token and the previous token; weak self-attention
heads.writes: Copies assorted tokens, mostly ellipses and rare word pieces; weak
heads.note: Self-attention 0.17 and copying score +0.87 in OV·S, but the copied tokens lack a common theme; the card gives little to go on.

heads.fires: Adverbs of degree 'how', 'more', 'most', 'very' before an adjective
heads.attends: The previous token, often an intensifier or 'just'
heads.writes: Boosts degree words and superlatives like 'more', 'most', 'very', 'high', 'best'
heads.note: Contexts show 'just how' + adjective and 'ultra tidy'; OV·S copies 'more', 'most', 'very', 'higher'; prev-token attention 0.17.

heads.fires: Garbled or unknown characters (replacement glyphs) in CJK text
heads.attends: Earlier occurrences of the same token (duplicate-token attention)
heads.writes: Weak output; no clear promoted tokens
heads.note: Duplicate-token attention 0.36 and self-seeking z +3.89; contexts show repeated replacement characters; OV output is weak (copy score +0.09).

heads.fires: Phrasal verb particles and prepositions ending a verb phrase ('with', 'for', 'from', 'in')
heads.attends: The verb or the previous token that governs a preposition
heads.writes: Copies prepositions and modal-like words such as 'most', 'what', 'through', 'concerned'
heads.note: Contexts show prepositions after verbs ('came up with', 'look out for', 'come from'); copies 'most', 'what', 'through'; prev-token 0.17.

heads.fires: Word-initial fragments and split word pieces inside compound words
heads.attends: Previous token; closing quotes and brackets as keys
heads.writes: Weak promotion of word-start fragments like 'dup', 'stri', 'sur'
heads.note: Drivers are word-start fragments; copy score +0.42 but OV·R weak and attention diffuse.

heads.fires: Tokens inside code string escapes and tab sequences
heads.attends: The previous token, with weak self-attention
heads.writes: Copies backslashes, tab-escape strings and some function words
heads.note: OV·S copies '\' and tab escapes; previous-token attention 0.21; the evidence is thin and mixed.

heads.fires: whitespace-indent and tab runs, and mid-word fragments in code/text
heads.attends: content nouns in lists (albums, decks, recipes, screenings), plural topic words
heads.writes: copies content nouns and topic words; suppresses punctuation and function words
heads.note: Driver list is whitespace runs; OV·S copies many content nouns and suppresses punctuation/articles; contexts are weak and mixed.

heads.fires: non-English words in multilingual text (Arabic, Thai, Korean, Vietnamese, Hungarian)
heads.attends: non-English content words and proper nouns in foreign-language passages
heads.writes: promotes Romance/Germanic and other non-English word fragments; copies foreign tokens
heads.note: OV·S copy list is dominated by French, Romanian, Dutch and similar tokens; drivers are scripts of many languages; weak layer-4 signal.

heads.fires: repeated-token positions, especially newline and ellipsis runs
heads.attends: earlier copies of the same token (duplicate-token attention)
heads.writes: suppresses ellipses, quotes and closing punctuation after newlines
heads.note: Duplicate score 0.12 and self-seeking z +1.52 mark a duplicate head; OV·R suppresses ellipsis and quote tokens.

heads.fires: gendered and school-related nouns (girl, women, feminist, school, students)
heads.attends: Harry Potter names and houses, and sports team nouns
heads.writes: promotes gendered nouns (women, girl, female, feminism) and Chinese female-related words
heads.note: OV·R copies women/girl/feminist tokens strongly; QK and drivers include Hogwarts/Potter and sports-team names; moderate confidence.

heads.fires: repeated closing-bracket runs and code/prose boundaries before a repeat
heads.attends: the token following an earlier copy of the current token (induction)
heads.writes: copies the continuation of repeated text; mild copy of prepositions and conjunctions
heads.note: Induction score 0.61 is high; OV·R copies 'and', 'the', 'of', 'to' while QK favours closing brackets and punctuation.

heads.fires: opening parentheses and brackets starting argument or tuple lists
heads.attends: opening parenthesis or bracket tokens, especially after a function name
heads.writes: copies closing parentheses and brackets, e.g. ')' and ')]'
heads.note: (recovered from malformed JSON)

heads.fires: closing brackets and parentheses in code, and 'or'/'and' between hyphen-linked words
heads.attends: closing parens and brackets after a repeated structure; hyphenated word parts
heads.writes: copies determiners and function words like 'the', 'a', 'in'; suppresses closing parens
heads.note: OV·S copies 'the' and closing brackets; OV·R suppresses ')' tokens; contexts show hyphen-pair continuations.

heads.fires: colons and commas before list-like or key names, and dialogue ellipses
heads.attends: sentence-initial words after ellipses or comma-led clauses
heads.writes: suppresses 'the', 'a', and spacing tokens; weak write overall
heads.note: Output norm is at the layer's minimum and OV·S is negative; labels rest on the suppression list and weak drivers.

heads.fires: fires on word-piece continuations inside split names and rare words (e.g. Ži|ž|ek, Z|iz|ou)
heads.attends: attends to the earlier fragment of a split multi-token word or name
heads.writes: weak copy of rare word-piece fragments; suppresses punctuation and function tokens
heads.note: Contexts show name fragments attended; OV copy list is mixed, suppression list is punctuation-heavy; layer 4 reads are weak.

heads.fires: fires on digits and tokens inside DOI numbers and citation strings
heads.attends: attends to the same digit or number token earlier in a DOI or code string
heads.writes: unclear; weakly suppresses names and sentence-internal words
heads.note: Few clear contexts (DOI digits); OV reads are near zero and mixed, so layer-4 writing is unclear.

heads.fires: fires on word-piece tails of split names and foreign surnames
heads.attends: attends to earlier fragments of the same split name
heads.writes: promotes ellipsis and quote-like continuations; suppresses names and 'there/here'
heads.note: Copy list leans toward '...' and ellipsis tokens; contexts are name-fragment splits, a weak pattern.

heads.fires: fires on math symbols and LaTeX-like tokens and on the query inside code-like or spelled strings
heads.attends: attends to the token itself, self-attending in mixed formulas and fragments
heads.writes: weakly promotes math symbols and digits; suppresses prose words
heads.note: Self-attention is the highest signal (0.21); OV copy list is digits and math symbols, but the copying score is near zero.

heads.fires: fires on sentence and clause endings and on closing parentheses before line breaks
heads.attends: attends to the preceding word in a list of connectives or quote-closing tokens
heads.writes: promotes sentence-level punctuation and dashes; suppresses dashes and connectives
heads.note: Drivers and QK reads are dominated by closing brackets and line breaks; the OV list is mixed.

heads.fires: fires on adverbs and particles that end reduplicated Chinese phrases (地, 的, 了)
heads.attends: attends to the first character of a repeated Chinese reduplication (緊緊, 靜靜, 慢慢)
heads.writes: promotes the particle 地/的 and Chinese adverb endings after reduplicated words
heads.note: Drivers and contexts clearly show adverb-particle completions in Chinese reduplication, the strongest pattern here.

heads.fires: fires on Chinese particles 了 and 当/如果 before a predicted completion
heads.attends: attends to earlier 了 or 和 and other Chinese connectives in the same clause
heads.writes: promotes Chinese quantity or completion words (许多, 半) after 了
heads.note: Contexts show 了 followed by 许多/半 completions; drivers also show 了 and 当/如果 clause starts.

heads.fires: fires on operators and code syntax tokens such as '=' and braces before a value
heads.attends: attends to earlier '{{' or repeated long whitespace runs in code and templates
heads.writes: weakly promotes 'the' and code operators; suppresses sentence-ending punctuation
heads.note: Drivers are '=' in code and key tokens are '{{' and whitespace runs; OV reads are weak at this layer.

heads.fires: mixed mid-text tokens; weak, diffuse firing with no clear theme
heads.attends: diffuse; no clear key class; weak attention to previous token
heads.writes: suppresses closing quotes and newlines after quotes or brackets
heads.note: OV·R suppresses newline-closed punctuation ("⏎⏎, })⏎) while copying closing-quote forms; QK and drivers are unclear, layer 4 weak band.

heads.fires: tokens before a verb or function word in running prose; diffuse
heads.attends: spacing and space-prefixed tokens, common function words like 'the', 'didn'
heads.writes: weakly suppresses quotes, brackets and line-break tokens
heads.note: QK favours space tokens and contraction stems; OV·R is weakly negative; layer 4 is weak band, low confidence.

heads.fires: tokens in code and prose where a following word is predicted; diffuse
heads.attends: closing brackets and parentheses before newlines in code
heads.writes: suppresses closing quotes and sentence-final punctuation before newlines
heads.note: QK strongly favours ')) ]' closers and '}")' endings; OV·R suppresses closing quotes; weak evidence.

heads.fires: capitalised abbreviation-like tokens (single letters, two-letter codes)
heads.attends: uppercase single-letter or code tokens, e.g. 'KG', 'YP', '	' indent
heads.writes: suppresses function words like 'that', 'in', 'of' and ellipses
heads.note: Drivers and key tokens are uppercase code-like pairs; OV·R suppresses common function words; layer 4 weak.

heads.fires: whitespace and indentation runs in code, and newline-heavy blank lines
heads.attends: indentation whitespace tokens and newline-indent runs
heads.writes: suppresses British spellings and words like 'colour', 'organised'
heads.note: Drivers and keys are indent whitespace; OV·R suppresses British -ise/-our forms, OV·S is negative on copying.

heads.fires: Chinese place names and Australian/Commonwealth proper names
heads.attends: place and proper names like Australian cities, Chinese provinces, nationalities
heads.writes: copies British spellings such as 'organised', 'colour', 'recognised'
heads.note: OV·R copies -ise/-our British spellings strongly; drivers are Chinese city and admin names; moderate confidence.

heads.fires: Chinese and English phrases following a comma or dash in prose
heads.attends: dashes and contrastive connectives like 'However', 'Furthermore'
heads.writes: copies em-dashes and connective adverbs; suppresses contraction endings
heads.note: OV·R copies dash-prefixed tokens and suppresses ’s/’t contraction suffixes; QK diffuse; weak band.

heads.fires: long whitespace-indent tokens and setter/getter method names in code
heads.attends: method-name tokens like getType, setOutput, and indent runs
heads.writes: suppresses quotes and British-spelling stems, weakly
heads.note: Drivers are long space runs and .set/.get method tokens; output-side reads are weak and noisy.

heads.fires: Mid-sentence after Chinese 我们/你/我 pronoun openers, and after word-stems like 'ers' or 'businesses'
heads.attends: Pronoun-start tokens in Chinese text and code-closing brackets with newlines
heads.writes: Weak pronoun copying (you/they/we, 你/我们) into the residual
heads.note: OV·R copies pronouns (your, they, we, 你的, 我们) but drivers are weak and QK reads are bracket-newline tokens; mixed evidence.

heads.fires: Inside code or citation strings after a repeated run of quotes, dashes, or journal-name tokens
heads.attends: Long runs of repeated quote or dash padding tokens
heads.writes: Suppresses paragraph-break tokens like ⏎⏎ and ellipses
heads.note: OV·R suppresses ⏎⏎ and ellipsis tokens strongly; drivers are scattered, so the firing context is weakly supported.

heads.fires: Superlative and determiner positions (-est, most, any, those) in English prose
heads.attends: Superlative stems and prior-context modifiers like 'most', 'largest'
heads.writes: Promotes ellipsis and newline-run tokens like ...⏎⏎
heads.note: OV·R copies ellipsis and ⏎⏎ runs; contexts show superlatives as the attended-to tokens and the query at the adjective end.

heads.fires: Dot or domain separators inside URLs and code, and 'in' or 'the' before noun phrases
heads.attends: Domain-name dot tokens and preceding path segments
heads.writes: Weak promotion of slash and newline tokens
heads.note: Contexts mostly show .org/.it after domain stems; OV reads are noisy and unclear.

heads.fires: Adjective or adverb positions in English prose and in technical list items
heads.attends: Evaluative adjectives and intensifiers such as large, key, critical, unprecedented
heads.writes: Copies evaluative adjectives and adverbs like gradually, extremely, dangerous
heads.note: OV·S and OV·R both copy adjectives and adverbs strongly (percentile 97); drivers show intensifier-adjective prefixes like 史上最.

heads.fires: Inside Django and Qt identifiers after a framework stem like rest_ or INSTALLED_
heads.attends: Framework or library name tokens such as Qt, Django, MongoDB, tkinter
heads.writes: Copies religious and legal nouns like ministry, law, Bible
heads.note: Drivers are framework identifiers while OV·R copies religion and law nouns; the mapping between them is unclear.

heads.fires: Mid-sentence in 'WikiLeaks'-style named entities and after 'the' in code comments
heads.attends: Named entities and code-block boundary tokens
heads.writes: Suppresses excited-tone words like folks, vibes, gonna and emojis
heads.note: OV·S and OV·R both suppress informal and enthusiastic tokens, a consistent pattern across the card.

heads.fires: Interjections and exclamation marks at the end of emotive clauses
heads.attends: Exclamation and informal emphasis tokens such as !, really, stuff, gonna
heads.writes: Promotes exclamation marks and informal emphatic tokens like gonna, folks
heads.note: OV·R copies !, gonna, vibes, folks strongly (percentile 84); drivers are product and topic nouns with weak fit.

heads.fires: Fires on code/markup closers and punctuation before newlines, e.g. .setFont, .appendChild, ylabel calls
heads.attends: Attends to sentence-final punctuation and closing brackets before newlines (.⏎⏎, ).⏎, ”.)
heads.writes: Promotes diverse content tokens when reading them (weak copy); suppresses newline and bracket tokens
heads.note: Self-seeking and QK favour .⏎⏎ and ) tokens; OV copying score is moderate and theme is unclear; layer 5 band weak.

heads.fires: Fires on mid-number digits and identifiers inside repeated code strings like '123456'
heads.attends: Attends to newline-heavy sentence ends and itself (self-seeking on repeated tokens)
heads.writes: Suppresses whitespace and ellipsis tokens; weakly promotes words like 'now', 'right', 'here'
heads.note: Strong self-seeking (z +2.89) but OV reads weak and mixed; suppression of newline/ellipsis tokens is the clearest write.

heads.fires: Fires on content nouns and technical terms in mid-sentence (challenge, WikiLeaks, vaccines)
heads.attends: Attends to sentence-final content nouns and bare topical nouns in lists
heads.writes: Mildly promotes function words (in, the, to, and) and suppresses discourse words like right, just, now
heads.note: Copying score near zero; OV pattern is weak; QK favours technical nouns; layer 5 band unclear.

heads.fires: Fires on pronoun-like tokens such as We, Our, 我们, 你觉得 in first/second person framing
heads.attends: Attends to the previous token, often a dot or newline or the token before a method name
heads.writes: Copies first-person plural and possessive pronouns (We, Our, 我们) forward
heads.note: Highest output norm in layer; OV copying score +0.96 with we/our/我们 leading; drivers include 我们 and 你 phrases.

heads.fires: Fires on the second copy of a word inside a repeated phrase, e.g. the repeated 'normal', 'ying', 'isnan'
heads.attends: Attends to earlier occurrences of the same token (duplicate-token lookup)
heads.writes: Copies the repeated token's identity forward when it reappears, weakly
heads.note: Duplicate attention 0.54 and median self-seeking z +5.93 mark a duplicate-token head; copy effect is weak in OV.

heads.fires: Fires on topic-opening Chinese words like 详细, 我希望, 这篇文章 before answers
heads.attends: Attends to sentence and list-ending punctuation before newlines
heads.writes: Suppresses ellipsis and dot-run tokens while weakly copying content tokens
heads.note: Drivers are Chinese instruction-like words; OV evidence weak; suppression of ellipses is the clearest signal.

heads.fires: Fires on content words repeated later in the text, such as Ashes, _percent, 重, slash
heads.attends: Attends to earlier copies of the current token (duplicate-token lookup)
heads.writes: Weakly copies function words and ellipses forward (the, a, ...)
heads.note: Duplicate attention 0.14 and self-seeking z +5.87 suggest duplicate detection; OV copying modest.

heads.fires: Fires on mid-word fragments of multi-token words, e.g. Bio|informatics, Dept, 规律
heads.attends: Attends to itself and the sink; mostly quiet on other tokens
heads.writes: Suppresses math and bracket tokens; weak copying of ellipsis and newline tokens
heads.note: Self-attention 0.30 and negative self-seeking; drivers are word fragments; write effects weak.

heads.fires: closing brackets/braces and code-like punctuation runs, after code or prose
heads.attends: previous-line or newline-heavy tokens; weak, diffuse key choice
heads.writes: promotes closing brackets and parentheses like ')}' and '))'
heads.note: OV·S copy list is dominated by closing brackets ')}', '))', '])'; OV·R is mixed, suppresses newline-run tokens; attention pattern is low on all scores.

heads.fires: long runs of repeated symbols or spaces (rules, padding lines)
heads.attends: paragraph-end punctuation followed by newlines ('.\n\n')
heads.writes: promotes closing brackets and braces; suppresses padding and repeated-space tokens
heads.note: Drivers as query are long dash/hash/space runs; OV·S copies closing brackets; weak pattern scores, mid-layer.

heads.fires: long divider-line tokens of dashes, stars, hashes, and spaces
heads.attends: previous divider or whitespace-run tokens
heads.writes: unclear; weak promotion of common mid-sentence words and '\n'
heads.note: Drivers and self-seeking favor divider runs, but OV reads are weak and mixed; low output norm.

heads.fires: long divider and padding runs, and code-line starts
heads.attends: unclear; weak preference for prior quote-and-newline endings
heads.writes: weak promotion of function words like 'and', 'in', 'the'
heads.note: OV·R copies common function words such as 'and' and 'in'; suppresses ellipsis-newline runs; otherwise diffuse.

heads.fires: quantifier and determiner words: 'many', 'some', 'every', 'this', 'these'
heads.attends: sentence-initial quantifier or demonstrative words ('These', 'Some', 'One')
heads.writes: promotes quantifiers and determiners ('many', 'some', 'all', 'each')
heads.note: Drivers include Chinese 那/这 determiners and quantifiers; OV·S copies quantifiers like 'all', 'some', 'every'.

heads.fires: time-separator colons and digits in timestamps, and CR-newline boundaries
heads.attends: earlier occurrence of the same token (duplicate, strong at 0.81)
heads.writes: unclear; OV·S suppresses copies of its attended tokens
heads.note: Duplicate score 0.81 is the clearest signal; self-seeking z high; OV reads are weak, and the layer is mid-band.

heads.fires: word-position tokens inside titles or topic phrases ('Airport', 'beauty', 'logistics')
heads.attends: earlier copies of the current word (duplicate, 0.25) and noun-phrase heads
heads.writes: weak promotion of common words like 'one', 'clean', 'expression'
heads.note: Duplicate score moderate and self-seeking high; OV reads mostly unclear at this depth.

heads.fires: auxiliary and modal verbs after a subject ('will', 'would', 'was', 'could')
heads.attends: the subject or noun before the modal, in clauses about events
heads.writes: promotes auxiliary and modal verbs: 'was', 'would', 'will', 'had'
heads.note: Drivers and OV·R/OV·S copies consistently point to modals and past auxiliaries; the key side is less clear.

heads.fires: Mid-token inside word or code/CJK fragments after closing brackets and newlines; diffuse
heads.attends: Previous token; broad, weak mix of prior punctuation and word pieces
heads.writes: Boosts closing brackets and punctuation (), ], }, ）, ”) while suppressing content words
heads.note: Previous-token pattern (0.39); OV·S copies closing brackets and quotes strongly; QK favours newline-punctuation keys. Layer-5 band, so weak.

heads.fires: Sentence-final and clause-boundary tokens, weak and broad
heads.attends: Previous token and sink; no clear key class
heads.writes: Mildly copies brackets and math tokens; little clear promotion
heads.note: Low-norm head with no sharp attention or OV theme; layer-5 signal is weak.

heads.fires: Comma and dash tokens before clause continuations (,— , ,\ )
heads.attends: Previous token and opening-bracket/quote-adjacent tokens in code
heads.writes: Copies closing parentheses and brackets like ) ] ）; suppresses indentation and CJK fillers
heads.note: Previous-token weight 0.30; OV·S copies closing-paren tokens; contexts show comma and dash firing.

heads.fires: Comma and dash clause tokens and code separators like ,\ and ,temp
heads.attends: Previous token and space/indent tokens
heads.writes: Copies opening brackets and quotes like ( { ‘; suppresses closing punctuation
heads.note: OV·S copies brackets and quotes; contexts show quote and dash firings, but evidence is modest.

heads.fires: Verb stems and bare-word positions before a continuation, like 'help', 'know', 'said'
heads.attends: Previous token; for code, opening markup tags and the colon in timestamps
heads.writes: Copies bare verb and base-form tokens (know, make, help, given); suppresses punctuation and indentation
heads.note: OV·S copying score +0.96 at percentile 94; copies base verbs strongly, and OV·R also copies verb-like words.

heads.fires: Word-initial fragments of compounds and prefixes like multi-, pre-, full-, sub-
heads.attends: Previous token and bracket openers in code such as [% and [$
heads.writes: Copies prefix fragments like pre, sub, multi, full, Trans; suppresses ellipses and pronouns
heads.note: OV·S copies prefix tokens (pre×3, sub×4, Trans×3); drivers are compound prefixes like multi and full.

heads.fires: Acronyms and all-caps tokens (BJP, MCC, IMF) and the 'know' tokens after 'I'
heads.attends: Opening brackets and braces in code, [[ and ${
heads.writes: Suppresses copying of hedging adverbs and quote closers; little clear promotion
heads.note: OV·R copy score -0.25 (suppressive); acronym drivers and bracket keys, layer-5 weak read.

heads.fires: Action verbs in participle or base form (get, found, use, applying, put, places)
heads.attends: Previous token and code method calls like .writeFile, .drawText
heads.writes: Copies verb forms (get, use, check, add, learn); suppresses determiners and articles
heads.note: OV·S copies verb tokens (get, found, done, use); drivers are verb-like words and method-call names.

heads.fires: Mid-phrase tokens inside multi-token words or after a name; diffuse, weak firing
heads.attends: Previous-token-ish content; no clear single key class
heads.writes: Weakly copies assorted word-piece and code tokens; little coherent promotion
heads.note: Low sink/prev-token scores; OV copy score near zero with mixed token lists; layer-5 band is weak evidence.

heads.fires: Second and later pieces of split names or words (e.g. 'Ch', 'Pir', 'Carp|al')
heads.attends: Opening parenthesis or bracket tokens and split-word continuations
heads.writes: Mildly promotes copies of word-fragment tokens; suppresses closing brackets
heads.note: Contexts show mid-word splits; QK favours code closers; OV copies fragments and suppresses ')' and newline tokens.

heads.fires: Number-words and digits in numeric or enumerated contexts (thirty, forty, 2, 3)
heads.attends: Mid-word or mid-phrase tokens in the preceding few words, e.g. 'Pass⟪ive⟫'
heads.writes: Promotes number tokens and digits; suppresses ellipsis and hedge words
heads.note: Drivers as query are decade and digit words; OV copying score is slightly negative, so writes are weak.

heads.fires: Quoted or bracketed names and tokens inside spans such as 'Barn⟪es⟫' or 'Nuts'
heads.attends: Opening quotes, brackets and sentence-initial tokens
heads.writes: Suppresses its own copies; weakly promotes ellipsis and bracket tokens
heads.note: Copy score negative; drivers include numeric words like 五百 and name-continuations; evidence is thin.

heads.fires: Tokens right before a line break or after '","' list punctuation in code or JSON
heads.attends: Newline and paragraph-break tokens and list-separator punctuation
heads.writes: Promotes newline and paragraph-end tokens; mild copy of list punctuation
heads.note: Strong QK on paragraph-break tokens; drivers are '","' and '":[' list separators; OV copies some plain function words.

heads.fires: Negation and scope words like 不仅, 只是, 即使 and 'not only' before the clause
heads.attends: Following clause-openers and sentence-starting words like 'Also', 'Moreover', 'Finally'
heads.writes: Promotes scope-modifying words (not, but, than, even, just) in copy
heads.note: Drivers are Chinese negation-scope phrases; OV copies 'not', 'even', 'just', 'but' strongly.

heads.fires: Conditional and purpose openers: 如果, 无论, 为什么不, 为了避免
heads.attends: Opening brackets and braces in code such as '{{' and '[{'
heads.writes: Promotes conditional and concessive words (If, Thus, As, When, 如果)
heads.note: Drivers are conditional Chinese openers; OV copies 'If', 'As', 'When', 'should'; QK favours brace and template tokens.

heads.fires: Country, nationality and city names (China, French, Indian, Canadian)
heads.attends: Nationality and place-name adjectives earlier in the text
heads.writes: Copies nationality and country adjectives (French, Chinese, British, Indian)
heads.note: Drivers and OV·R copies are dominated by nationality and country names; OV·S copies place names like Caribbean, Indonesia.

heads.fires: closing brackets and quotes ending a clause, e.g. )) and ”), in Chinese and English
heads.attends: sentence-initial quote-opening tokens and bracket openers, e.g. “She, “They, ([
heads.writes: weak copy of whitespace and closing-bracket tokens; suppresses closing parens
heads.note: Self-seeking median is modest; copy list is mixed whitespace and closers; QK favours closing brackets; little clear theme, low confidence.

heads.fires: Chinese and code tokens after verbs or nouns where a continuation is about to start
heads.attends: Chinese noun-phrase starts like 的女孩, 和他的, and code calls like (TEXT
heads.writes: unclear; weakly promotes math and symbol tokens, suppresses assorted Chinese words
heads.note: Drivers and key contexts are heterogeneous; OV reads are weak with no strong theme.

heads.fires: Chinese prepositions 在, 为, 对, 把 before an object phrase
heads.attends: the preposition-plus-object structure in Chinese, e.g. 为客户, 将自己的
heads.writes: promotes function words like As, When, How, What; suppresses punctuation and quotes
heads.note: Drivers are consistently Chinese prepositions 为/对/在/把; copy list has sentence-opening wh-words and prepositions.

heads.fires: tokens inside path or delimiter strings, e.g. ','=', ./, :[", ('/')
heads.attends: Chinese 的/和 noun-phrase joints and code delimiters like ('../', [parent
heads.writes: promotes sentence-ending punctuation like ! and ? and period tokens
heads.note: Drivers mix code delimiters with Chinese joiners; copy list is punctuation-led, moderate confidence.

heads.fires: auxiliary and past-tense verbs like will, would, was, had after a subject
heads.attends: past-time adverbs and time phrases such as 当时, 昨晚, 去年, recently
heads.writes: promotes auxiliary and past-tense verbs: was, would, had, were
heads.note: Strong, consistent copy list of auxiliaries and past-tense verbs; key contexts show time words and had/were.

heads.fires: tokens inside code or noun compounds, e.g. bombings, doping, debugging, 研究生
heads.attends: Chinese adjective 的 phrases and nouns followed by 的, e.g. 最重要的, 自己的
heads.writes: suppresses past-tense verbs and ellipsis; weak negative copy
heads.note: Writes are mostly suppression of was/had and ellipses; firing is diffuse across nouns.

heads.fires: code-like delimiters and whitespace-indent runs, e.g. ','=', ⏎    ⏎
heads.attends: Chinese and English topical nouns like 历史, 质量, 协会 and code method names
heads.writes: promotes Chinese and quote-closing punctuation like ”， and ,”; suppresses auxiliaries
heads.note: OV copies closing quotes and commas; suppresses was, will, could; moderate-weak evidence.

heads.fires: code attribute dots and delimiters, e.g. .Adapter, .Sprite, ','=','
heads.attends: plural nouns of groups and history, e.g. historians, ancestors, scriptures
heads.writes: suppresses ellipsis and closing-quote tokens; weakly copies function words
heads.note: Self-seeking is strong in closers; drivers are code dots; writes suppress ellipsis closers.

heads.fires: Nouns in Chinese/English topical phrases (festivals, professions, hobbies, parenting), mid-sentence
heads.attends: Code-ish and tokens like ')))⏎⏎', 'controller', 'frame', 'canvas' (QK-favoured keys)
heads.writes: Copies topical content nouns (doctors, children, prayer, festivals) forward into output
heads.note: OV·R copy list is thematic (medical, children, religion, relationships); fire contexts weak and mixed; layer 6 band, moderate reliability.

heads.fires: Positions after a sentence-internal token where a function word or comma follows; high-norm but diffuse
heads.attends: Sentence-ending closers and code block tokens like ')))⏎', '。⏎⏎'
heads.writes: Suppresses topical nouns (children, students, doctors) and function-word-like tokens; mild negative copy
heads.note: OV·R suppresses topical nouns and copies function words; self-attention high (0.44); unclear role, layer 6 weak band.

heads.fires: Tokens inside a multi-token word or name at the position just before a continuation, e.g. '網 (2013-04-10⟦⟧09'
heads.attends: Words in the middle of a multi-token name or title ('International', 'Journal', 'Political')
heads.writes: Copies generic content words and code-start tokens; suppresses 'the' and punctuation
heads.note: Contexts show mid-name tokens attended; OV reads diffuse and weak, so writing is a guess.

heads.fires: Content nouns after a sentence-opening or topic word, such as '酒', '报警', '奶茶', 'Stack' in topical text
heads.attends: Tokens of a multi-word title or citation, e.g. 'Law', 'Mathematical', 'Political', 'lung'
heads.writes: Copies nouns about health, children and education; suppresses digits and capital single letters
heads.note: Contexts consistently attend to the first word of a journal or title name; OV-R copy list is thematic, suppresses digits and letters.

heads.fires: Positions inside code or quoted strings and in rare Chinese tokens (e.g. '天空部落', '電話及')
heads.attends: Tokens in identifiers or alphabetic fragments like 'TRI', 'Cec', 'ISA', 'alph'
heads.writes: Suppresses runs of whitespace and ellipsis tokens; copies rare traditional-Chinese fragments
heads.note: OV-R suppresses whitespace indentation and ellipses, copies disclaimers-like traditional Chinese; contexts mixed; low norm.

heads.fires: Second item of a paired antonym or month/name sequence, e.g. '⟦Nov⟧', '⟦ly⟧', '⟦pos⟧'
heads.attends: The first half of a parallel pair: '⟪Oct⟫', '⟪pt⟫', '⟪uly⟫', '⟪_neg⟫', '黑白'
heads.writes: Predicts the completion of a parallel pair or sequence (months, opposites, 'and/but' connectives)
heads.note: Contexts pair a first-half token with a second-half token in month lists and antonym pairs; OV copies connectives weakly.

heads.fires: Tokens inside a sequence of abbreviation-like or name-like fragments, e.g. '1⟪1⟫', 'International', '马⟦·⟧'
heads.attends: Early tokens of multi-token names or titles (International, 'st', 'Jul')
heads.writes: Copies month abbreviations and Chinese surnames; suppresses 'is', 'with', punctuation
heads.note: OV·S copy list has months and surnames; contexts show name/title fragments; moderate-low confidence.

heads.fires: Repeated-character runs and separator tokens like '=====' and long whitespace or quote runs
heads.attends: Same-type long runs (whitespace, '=====', dashes) and sentence-start tokens after 'didn', 'couldn'
heads.writes: Copies whitespace and separator runs forward; suppresses 'in', 'is', and ordinary function words
heads.note: OV·S copies indentation runs and symbols; drivers are '=' separators; self-attention 0.42 on runs.

heads.fires: Mid-phrase tokens in code and mixed-script text; weak, diffuse firing
heads.attends: Previous token and closing-bracket or newline runs in code
heads.writes: Suppresses function words and modal adverbs; weak copy of assorted tokens
heads.note: Low sink and previous-token scores, no induction or duplicate signal; OV reads are mixed with no clear theme, so the write is a guess.

heads.fires: Hedging and emphasis words like 'should', 'may', 'often', 'also' in prose
heads.attends: Previous token; closing parenthesis and newline runs like '))⏎⏎'
heads.writes: Promotes adverbs and hedges such as 'sometimes', 'perhaps', 'probably'
heads.note: OV·R copy list is a clear adverb and hedge theme; drivers show Chinese discourse words; attend side is weak.

heads.fires: Indentation and whitespace-run tokens in code and repeated tokens
heads.attends: Itself: strongly attends to the current token (self-seeking)
heads.writes: Suppresses adverbs and hedges like 'often', 'some', 'rather'
heads.note: Self-attention 0.38 and high self-seeking z; OV·S copy score is negative, so it mostly suppresses prose adverbs.

heads.fires: Contrastive and transitional words such as 'However', 'Although', '但'
heads.attends: Previous token and subject-introducing words in clauses
heads.writes: Promotes adjectives and adverbs like 'useful', 'better', 'often'
