heads.note: Drivers are contrastive connectives; OV·S copies adjectives such as 'useful' and 'valuable'; weak overall.

heads.fires: Tokens after a word-start in code identifiers and names (e.g. '.internet', '(DIS')
heads.attends: Previous token, typically the immediately preceding token
heads.writes: Unclear; weak copy of mid-word and code identifier tokens
heads.note: Previous-token weight 0.28 is the strongest signal; the output reads are not consistent enough for a clear write.

heads.fires: Pronouns 'you', 'we', 'your' in English and Chinese first or second person
heads.attends: Preceding pronoun or first-person subject tokens like '我们' and 'you'
heads.writes: Promotes second-person and first-person pronouns such as 'your', 'you', '你的'
heads.note: OV·R copies 'your', 'you', '你' strongly and drivers are 我/你/我们 pronouns; consistent pronoun theme.

heads.fires: Subject pronouns and first-person clause starts like '我们', '我记得'
heads.attends: Previous token and code identifier names (library and class names)
heads.writes: Weak promotion of hedges and ellipsis like '...' and 'anyhow'
heads.note: Drivers mix first-person pronouns with library names; the output side is weak and mostly suppresses pronouns.

heads.fires: Mid-sentence tokens inside long clauses, often before a closing punctuation
heads.attends: Itself and the previous token; closing brackets like '))' in code
heads.writes: Suppresses second-person pronouns 'you' and 'your' and ellipsis
heads.note: Self-seeking median z 1.36 and self-attention 0.32; OV·R suppresses 'you/your', but overall signal is low.

heads.fires: on nouns/adjectives after a person-referent slot; strongest on words like 'Name', 'client', 'She' in mid-sentence
heads.attends: attends to the previous or nearby token, weakly tied to gendered/female referents
heads.writes: promotes female-gendered words (she, girl, woman, her, daughter)
heads.note: OV·R copies female words strongly (herself, girl, she, 她); the context firings are noisy and show referent tokens, so the write is the clearest signal.

heads.fires: on long runs of whitespace, dots and newline-padding tokens in code or layout
heads.attends: attends to code and whitespace tokens, e.g. indentation runs and comment markers
heads.writes: weakly promotes ellipsis and newline-padding tokens like '...⏎⏎'
heads.note: Drivers are indentation-space runs; OV·R copies '...⏎⏎' and newline tokens; the OV·S copy score is near zero, so the write is unclear.

heads.fires: on tokens ending a repeated separator or dash/star line, and after 'God' in names of God
heads.attends: attends to long separator-line tokens (dashes, #, =) and to the token 'God'
heads.writes: suppresses female-gendered words (she, girl, her, woman) when reading them
heads.note: OV·R suppresses she/girl/woman strongly; the head is a negative-copy head, so its write pushes away from female words.

heads.fires: on abstract plural nouns like 'aspects', 'problems', 'conditions' in analytic prose
heads.attends: attends to plural abstract nouns and 'of the' noun-phrase heads
heads.writes: promotes plural abstract nouns such as problems, conditions, aspects, things
heads.note: OV·S copies level, systems, conditions, aspects, values; OV·R copies Problems, areas, versions; a plural-abstract-noun theme.

heads.fires: on surnames and proper names at name-list positions, and comma/newline runs
heads.attends: attends to punctuation and newline tokens after clauses
heads.writes: suppresses expressive slang and emphatic dash words when reading them
heads.note: Heavy negative OV·R and OV·S with suppression lists of slang; firings are scattered across names and punctuation, so weakly evidenced.

heads.fires: on verbs and adjectives after 'I' or in promissory phrasing, e.g. 'promise', 'worth'
heads.attends: attends to the subject pronoun or verb 'promise' and neighbouring words
heads.writes: promotes emphatic dash-led adjectives and clause-continuing words
heads.note: OV·R copies dash-prefixed words like —we, —if and intensifiers; the context firings are mixed.

heads.fires: on digits and short code tokens inside numeric or identifier strings
heads.attends: attends to capitalised names and identifier-like tokens in code
heads.writes: weakly copies digit tokens and spacing tokens
heads.note: OV·S copies digits 1-9 and indentation runs; the firings are sparse and the attended key set is diffuse.

heads.fires: on tokens inside DOI and numeric identifiers, e.g. digits after '10.1'
heads.attends: attends to the digits and slashes of DOI or citation-number strings
heads.writes: promotes digit continuations and identifier-like tokens after a number
heads.note: Context examples are DOI digits split across tokens; OV·S is near neutral, so the write label is a weak guess.

heads.fires: Fires on prepositions and articles mid-phrase, e.g. 'towards the', 'for a', 'from a'
heads.attends: Attends to the sink (position 0) and to a word after a preposition
heads.writes: Weak copy of diverse content words and Chinese terms; no clear promoted token
heads.note: Sink-heavy (0.44); copying score high on OV·S but top copy list is heterogeneous; contexts show prepositions/articles; layer-7 band, weak evidence.

heads.fires: Fires on the token inside a list of nouns or a colon-introduced question word, unclear
heads.attends: Attends mostly to the sink position 0
heads.writes: Suppresses sentence-final tokens like '.⏎⏎' and closing brackets
heads.note: Sink 0.28; OV·R suppresses paragraph-end tokens; self-seeking is for '.⏎⏎' style tokens; drivers are topic nouns; weak.

heads.fires: Fires on code or math tokens and on repeated paragraph-ending tokens
heads.attends: Attends to the sink and itself (self-attention 0.21)
heads.writes: Suppresses topical nouns about games, feminism and sports
heads.note: Sink 0.36, self 0.21; OV·R suppresses topic words such as shit, Game, feminism; self-seeking mildly high; unclear.

heads.fires: Fires on capitalised proper nouns and names of teams, games or products
heads.attends: Attends to the sink; drivers show proper-name keys like regex, GraphQL, geometry
heads.writes: Promotes copies of education and school words such as teachers, school, students
heads.note: OV·R copy list is school/teacher/feminist themed; drivers are tech and sports names; moderate sink attention.

heads.fires: Fires on mid-word subword fragments in code and Chinese text
heads.attends: Attends almost entirely to the sink position 0
heads.writes: Near-null output; weakly suppresses dash and quote punctuation
heads.note: Sink 0.95 and small output norm (percentile 3); acts as a parked head with little effect.

heads.fires: Fires on repeated word-piece tokens inside identifiers, e.g. '_ex' and '_country' in code
heads.attends: Attends to the earlier occurrence of the current token (duplicate-token)
heads.writes: Suppresses repeated ellipses and em-dash tokens
heads.note: Duplicate score 0.92 and self-seeking z +4.4; contexts show it attending to the earlier copy of a repeated subword.

heads.fires: Fires on digits and math symbols such as 6, 4, 1, ${, frac
heads.attends: Attends to the sink, with some attention to repeated digits and identifier fragments
heads.writes: Weakly promotes digits and math symbols
heads.note: OV·S copies digits and LaTeX tokens; sink 0.96; contexts show digit and short-token repeats; weak.

heads.fires: Fires on repeated tokens inside code identifiers and dotted method names
heads.attends: Attends to earlier occurrences of the same token (duplicate-token), mostly sink otherwise
heads.writes: Suppresses ellipsis and closing punctuation tokens
heads.note: Duplicate score 0.55 and self-seeking z +4.3; OV·R suppresses ellipsis; drivers are dotted code names.

heads.fires: closing brackets and parens after code or quoted text, and newline-run tokens like .⏎⏎
heads.attends: the attention sink at position 0; little content-specific lookback
heads.writes: suppresses content words and ellipsis-like tokens; mildly copies closing brackets
heads.note: Sink-heavy (0.63). Copy list is closing brackets and punctuation; suppress list is content words and code idents. Weak, mixed signal.

heads.writes: Mild, unclear output; slight promotion of word-stem continuations, little clear effect
heads.note: Sink-dominant (0.76); OV copying score negative; contexts show digit tokens but evidence is weak at this depth.

heads.fires: Mid-sentence positions in academic prose before abstract nouns like structure, process, restriction
heads.attends: Attention sink (position 0) with weak pull toward abstract academic words
heads.writes: Suppresses abstract nouns such as structure, restricting, process, forming
heads.note: Strongly suppressive OV (score -0.97); suppresses 'structure', 'restricting', 'processes' when read, a copy-suppression pattern.

heads.fires: Tokens of noun-heavy technical or topical phrases (Research, Design, Quality, Construction)
heads.attends: Attention sink, with some self-attention; weak tie to nouns like structure and process
heads.writes: Copies abstract academic nouns such as structure, process, proper, mechanism
heads.note: Copying score +0.94, top copied tokens are structure, proper, process, mechanism, notion; a copying head for abstract nouns.

heads.fires: Symbol and special-character tokens (currency, quotes, zero-width spaces)
heads.attends: Previous token and sink; weak match to boilerplate phrases like 'This is a' or 'is a kind of'
heads.writes: Suppresses specification, constraint, precision, and structured technical nouns
heads.note: Copying score -0.73; suppresses technical nouns like specification and constraint; drivers are mostly symbols.

heads.fires: Sentence-start tokens of multi-syllable word fragments, often in Chinese or code context
heads.attends: Attention sink; weak focus on discourse connectives like Moreover and However
heads.writes: Suppresses nature and agriculture nouns (water, air, farm, food, gold)
heads.note: Copying score -0.80; suppresses water, farm, food, air tokens; the suppressive list is thematic.

heads.fires: Word-internal fragments inside multi-token words, especially the -ance/-ity/-ate endings
heads.attends: Attention sink; weak focus on discourse and sentence-linking words
heads.writes: Suppresses air, water, vegetable, and aviation nouns
heads.note: Copying score -0.57; suppresses water, air, vegetable, aviation tokens, a thematic suppression pattern similar to L35h20.

heads.fires: Whitespace-run tokens and spacing characters such as nbsp, tabs and carriage returns
heads.attends: Keyword-like nouns (sildenafil, viagra, cannabinoids, hypertension), attended from the query
heads.writes: Copies water, air, food and vehicle nouns (air, water, farm, seafood, airlines)
heads.note: Copying score +0.88; top copies are air, water, food, vehicle, and sports nouns; the attention-target list is a different health/drug theme.

heads.fires: Whitespace and special-character tokens (nbsp, zero-width, tabs) and partial-word fragments
heads.attends: Health, drug and food-topic plural nouns (homosexuality, cannabinoids, hypertension, vegetables)
heads.writes: Copies air, water, food and medical nouns (air, seafood, Drug, medical, cuisine)
heads.note: Copying score +0.86; copied tokens are air, food, water, medical; attention targets lean toward health and lifestyle nouns.

heads.fires: Mid-word fragments of long technical or Latinate words, e.g. MULT, interpre, explo
heads.attends: Sink position 0; as keys, plural role nouns like stakeholders, proponents, Participants
heads.writes: Mildly suppresses short code-identifier fragments like =z, ,J, [z
heads.note: Sink-heavy (0.56) with weak, mixed read lists; the suppression side is the clearest signal. Layer 35 reads are fairly reliable but the theme is diffuse.

heads.fires: Uppercase code or acronym prefixes like _APPRO, _PRO, _INTER, QUI, DEVELO
heads.attends: Uppercase keys, alphabet strings and capitalized name or Qt-class tokens
heads.writes: Promotes uppercase two-letter name fragments (JO, GW, WI); suppresses number words like Two, Three, As
heads.note: Copy score is positive; the copy list is uppercase fragments and suppression is spelled-out numbers. Drivers are uppercase code tokens in real text.

heads.fires: Word-start fragments like aut, mult, appro, descri, overwhel in mid-word positions
heads.attends: Sink; as keys, runs of repeated letters or alphabet strings like fffffff, abcdef
heads.writes: Suppresses digits and number words (0, nine, Thirty, zero, 8); copies random consonant fragments
heads.note: Strong suppression of numerals with a high-norm output (percentile 97). The copy side is random lowercase fragments, so the suppression is the reliable part.

heads.fires: Letter 'p' or '.m.' after clock times, and punctuation following numerals
heads.attends: Plural nouns for people or groups: stakeholders, NGOs, organisations, participants
heads.writes: Promotes digits and number words (0, 9, Two, Three); suppresses uppercase name fragments (JO, Zen, WO)
heads.note: Copies numerals and suppresses name-like uppercase tokens. Firings on time and range punctuation near numbers suggest a numeric-context head.

heads.fires: Digits inside numbers and years, e.g. the 0 in 1,000,000 and 2 in 2006
heads.attends: Sink; as keys, plural abstract nouns like inconsistencies, disagreements, beauty
heads.writes: Copies common function words and punctuation (and, in, of, to, the, period)
heads.note: Copy list is function words and punctuation with moderate score; the digit-context firings come from the top-firing contexts.

heads.fires: Digits in years and version strings (2006, 2017), and control or whitespace characters
heads.attends: Sink; as keys, end-of-block markers like }))⏎⏎ and -------⏎⏎
heads.writes: Copies whitespace and control characters; suppresses for/to/can/Canvas-type tokens (_FOR, To, can)
heads.note: Sink 0.79 with weak signals. The clearest firings are year digits; suppression is preposition and 'can' stems.

heads.fires: Negative contractions as query: didn, couldn, wouldn, doesn, isn
heads.attends: Sink; as keys, Chinese prepositions 对, 对于, 为 and English 'for'
heads.writes: Promotes 'for', 'to', 'of', 'on' and 对于-style prepositions
heads.note: Copy list is clearly prepositional (for, to, of, on, 对于); sink 0.90 means it acts rarely, mainly on contraction tokens.

heads.note: Copy list is modal verbs (Can, WILL, 可以, 会); the suppression is weaker. Date-digit firings from contexts are a secondary signal.
